The 188.5 d signal is not removed by a 1-planet model, so the data clearly need more than one planet. The residuals still show the same 188.5 d peak, which means the single-planet fit is incomplete and the dominant signal likely needs a more flexible multi-planet model to absorb it. However, the only other notable structure is at 0.6–1.4 d and near the cadence window, which looks like aliases/windowing rather than a clean second planet. The safest next hypothesis is still to keep 188.5 d as the primary planet and add the only other nontrivial long-period candidate, 88.37 d, because it is the only distinct longer-period peak not obviously tied to the daily window. - 188.51 d is the dominant, highly significant peak.

- A 1-planet model leaves very large residual scatter, so the system is definitely more complex than one planet.

I recommend the engineer fit a 2-planet model starting from these periods and check whether the 88.37 d signal survives after the long-period planet is modeled properly.
